entries.notes: Component-level power specs obtained: individual PZT transducers at 28–40 kHz rated at 50 W with coupling factor Kp ≥ 55%. For reactor scale, number of transducers would scale with desired acoustic intensity and vessel geometry — neither of which has a design basis for this concept. The key missing data point (electroacoustic wall-plug efficiency at system level) was not found in accessible sources; best available proxy is the manufacturer's coupling factor spec. The high-value ScienceDirect review paper is open-access but inaccessible to the extraction tool.

entries.notes: Key new finding: Hielscher search results surfaced wall-plug efficiency data (80-90% from plug to liquid) not found in prior iteration. This fills the gap left by the APC International source (which gave coupling coefficient Kp ≥ 55% but no wall-plug efficiency). The UIP16000 (16 kW, 18 kHz) and UIP4000hdT (4 kW, 20 kHz) together bracket the sonofusion operating frequency range and establish the per-unit power scale for commercial industrial ultrasonic systems. Reactor-scale estimation (GW-class) remains an analogy extrapolation: e.g., a 100 MWe acoustic driver load would require ~6,250 UIP16000 units at 16 kW each, illustrating the scale challenge.
